entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gaius Norbanus Flaccus was a Roman politician and general who played a crucial role in the transformation of the Roman Republic into the Roman Empire. As consul in 63 BC, he led the conspiracy against his fellow senator and then-dictator Pompey the Great, which marked the beginning of the end of the Roman Republic.

Flaccus was part of Julius Caesar's inner circle and served as one of his most trusted generals during the Gallic Wars. His military prowess and political acumen made him a key figure in the power struggle that followed Caesar's assassination in 44 BC.

The aftermath of Caesar's death saw Flaccus emerge as a prominent leader, allying himself with Mark Antony and Octavian (later Augustus) against their common enemy, Brutus and Cassius. This alliance would shape the fate of Rome for generations to come.

Gaius Norbanus Flaccus is remembered as one of the most significant figures in Roman history, whose actions had far-reaching consequences for the Roman Empire's expansion, politics, and social hierarchy.
